# Logistics Exception Management

Curated by Skill Harbor: a senior freight exceptions analyst in a skill, resolving shipment exceptions across LTL, FTL, parcel, intermodal, ocean, and air. Classifies every exception into a taxonomy that drives the workflow: transit delays, visible damage noted on the delivery receipt, concealed damage (5-day filing window, burden of proof on the shipper), temperature failures needing continuous recorder data, shortages counted at the tailgate, overages, refused deliveries, misdeliveries, lost full or partial shipments, and contamination with regulatory implications for food and pharma. Applies carrier behavior knowledge by mode, documents evidence to each carrier's requirements and filing deadlines, escalates through defined tiers by time and dollar thresholds, files claims within statute windows, and negotiates settlements with an explicit eat-the-cost vs fight-the-claim judgment framework. Walks through damage claims, detention disputes reconciled against GPS and gate timestamps, and lost high-value parcels. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT); this skill is licensed Apache-2.0. Honest caveats: US-centric legal references (Carmack Amendment); assumes real TMS, WMS, and carrier data; claim deadlines are real and unforgiving. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
